subject: Great Blue Heron age, 2026-09-20 — re-read from the less-synthetic frame
why: Entry 4 calls the bird "probably immature / first-year, ~65% confident" on a dark bill and a dark crown with no plumes. framing.py shows that read rests partly on IMG_3481, which is 272mm-equivalent on a phone with no telephoto — a ~10.5x upscale past the 2x sensor crop, where PROTOCOL.md 5a says the apparent detail is partly synthesised.

what_was_compared.verdict: USELESS for ageing — the bird is an unfocused smudge. The wide frame provides no independent check, which is itself worth knowing: there is no un-zoomed version of this observation to fall back on.
The most trustworthy usable frame. Shows a dark cap, a bill dark above and paler below, a pale foreneck with dark streaking, and no head plumes.
Looks sharper and carries no more real information. Nothing visible here is absent from IMG_3480.

conclusion: The immature read SURVIVES — IMG_3480 supports it as well as IMG_3481 did, so the conclusion was not an artefact of the upscale. But one of its two supporting arguments is weaker than Entry 4 implies: "no plumes" is poor evidence in late September, because an ADULT Great Blue Heron is in non-breeding plumage by then and has shed its breeding plumes too. The bill tone is doing nearly all the work. ~65% should be read as generous rather than conservative, and the honest confidence is lower.
recommendation: Leave Entry 4 as written — it is hedged, and the hedge is still right. Add this as a note when the season goes into the log. If an immature recurs at this mat, photograph it at 2x or closer, not at 10x.
